cosy-lesson.title: "None of us really have a choice in anything but we do have a choice to be ourselves. Stay free.": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Choice – the act of selecting or making a decision when faced with possibilities.

p.em: Example: We might not choose where we are born, but we always have a choice to stay true to our values.

cosy-blockquote.p: Freedom ≠ Captivity – the power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance or control ≠ the state of being imprisoned or confined.

p.em: Example: To stay free means to protect your individual mind from social expectations, avoiding cognitive captivity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the unique qualities, beliefs, and characteristics that make a person who they are.

p.em: Example: The constant pressure to conform can completely erase a person's individual identity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pressure – strong social influence or force that encourages someone to behave in a certain way.

p.em: Example: Many people feel intense pressure to follow traditional life paths.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conform – to adjust one's behavior or thinking to match the accepted standards of a group.

p.em: Example: When you choose to conform, you sacrifice a piece of your unique self-expression.

cosy-blockquote.p: Genuine – real, authentic, and true to one's own thoughts, feelings, and character.

p.em: Example: Living a genuine life brings a profound sense of inner peace and freedom.

cosy-blockquote.p: Decision – a conclusion or resolution reached after consideration and choosing among options.

p.em: Example: Every decision we make either moves us closer to our true self or further away.

cosy-blockquote.p: Independent – capable of thinking, deciding, and acting on one's own without relying on social approval.

p.em: Example: An independent mind is highly valuable in a world that rewards quiet conformity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Values – the important principles or beliefs that guide a person's behavior and choices.

p.em: Example: If you do not define your own values, others will happily define them for you.

cosy-blockquote.p: Expectations – the beliefs or demands of others regarding how we should behave or live.

p.em: Example: It is incredibly freeing to realize that you needn't live your life to meet others' expectations.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does the choice to stay genuine protect your mental wellness in a chaotic world?
★ Philosophers demand that we reflect deeply on life. Is it essential that everyone cultivate inner freedom?

Why do we often feel intense social pressure to meet others' heavy expectations?
★ Do you feel a need to perform or filter your true identity on social media?

What is the difference between having outward choices and possessing true inner freedom?
★ Can you feel a strong sense of freedom even when your life choices are limited?

In what areas of your life do you choose to conform, and where do you refuse to compromise?
★ Have you ever made a major life choice just to please social expectations?

Why is an independent thinker often viewed with suspicion or fear by traditional groups?
★ What part of your daily routine feels like a real, free choice to you?

How do your core personal values guide your behavior during moments of high stress?
★ Have you ever had to choose between showing loyalty and staying true to your own values?

How does moving away from family or familiar places help you discover your authentic identity?
★ What is the most important decision you made entirely by yourself as a teenager?

Is staying true to your own path a selfish act, or is it a necessary part of freedom?
★ In what area of your life do you feel you are most independent today?

What are the long-term consequences of constantly choosing to conform to avoid conflict?
★ How has your personal understanding of individual freedom shifted over the last five years?

If you could change one past decision to be more genuine, which one would it be?
★ If you had to describe your relationship with social pressure in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is it most difficult to stay free and remain genuine? Rank them: - 🏢 Career & Corporate Life When you must conform to strict corporate values and expectations to protect your job stability. - 🏡 Family Traditions & Rules When your parents' heavy expectations clash directly with your independent life choices. - 🌐 Online Networks & Media When peer pressure and digital likes push you to perform a fake persona rather than stay genuine. - 👥 Close Friends & Community When you must hide your authentic values to stay accepted in your core social circle.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will allow us to measure a person's genuine happiness with absolute precision. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if society began to filter and monitor your individual identity?

Modern digital algorithms will eventually destroy our collective capacity for independent decision-making. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use smart algorithms to make major career and relationship decision choices for you?

Future societies will prioritize individual freedom over traditional conformity and family rules. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with freedom?

As artificial intelligence advances, humans will face no pressure to work, giving them complete freedom of leisure. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic city, how would you protect citizens from the pressure of social expectations?

In the coming decades, choosing not to conform to digital norms will be seen as a highly positive trait. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where your core personal values are determined by online scores?

Future school systems will completely eliminate grades, allowing kids to learn purely based on personal choice. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think future kids will be more independent than today's children?

Future generations will look back at today's corporate conformity with deep skepticism and shock. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about the beauty of staying genuine to people 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make it incredibly difficult to maintain an independent lifestyle. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that guarantees physical safety at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by how genuine a person is rather than their wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope personal values will play in your own professional future over the next decade?

A future world governed fully by smart logic will leave no space left for the quiet mystery of individual identity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to exercise greater personal choice right now?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
